$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure Storage accounts. See aws/s3.json for the contract. One entry per console section (StorageAccountBlade.jsx MENU id).

azure.storage.account.crud.title: Storage accounts (create, get, list, delete) over ARM

azure.storage.containers.title: Containers (create, list, delete) over the Blob REST data plane
limitations: A container's anonymous access level (x-ms-blob-public-access: blob|container, set at create) is stored and echoed back on GetContainerProperties/ListContainers exactly as configured; enforcing it against a genuinely credential-less reader is not modelled (see azure.storage.configuration).

azure.storage.blobs.title: Blobs (upload, download, list, delete) over the Blob REST data plane
limitations: Every blob uploaded through the console is a block blob; page/append blobs are not simulated.

azure.storage.accesskeys.title: Access keys (the ARM listKeys action)
limitations: Keys are fixed simulator values, not real random key material, and Vyomi does not verify SharedKey request signatures against them.

azure.storage.endpoints.title: Endpoints
limitations: Only the Blob service endpoint is a live Vyomi URL; Data Lake Storage, File, Queue and Table endpoints shown are cosmetic (the Queue data plane is reachable at a different, unscoped path — see azure.storage.queues).

azure.storage.configuration.title: Configuration (performance, secure transfer, TLS, access tier, replication SKU, …)
limitations: ENFORCED: allowSharedKeyAccess=false really rejects a SharedKey-authenticated request (403 KeyBasedAuthenticationNotPermitted), and the Blob access tier (default) really seeds a newly uploaded blob's tier when the request carries no x-ms-access-tier of its own. Still config-only: HTTPS-only (secure transfer) and minimum TLS version have no real TLS negotiation layer underneath to enforce a protocol/version against, Entra-only portal auth is a console preference, and the permitted-scope-for-copy-operations restriction is not checked on copy.

azure.storage.redundancy.title: Redundancy (replication SKU)
limitations: ENFORCED: an RA-GRS/RA-GZRS sku really exposes a separate, read-only `{account}-secondary` Blob endpoint serving this account's own data; any other sku 404s it, and writes against it always 403. Still not simulated: actual geo-replication lag, a genuinely separate secondary-region store and customer-managed failover — Vyomi stores data once, locally.

azure.storage.networking.title: Networking (public network access / firewall default action / routing preference)
limitations: ENFORCED: publicNetworkAccess="Disabled" really rejects every Blob data-plane request for that account (403 AuthorizationFailure) — the account has no private endpoint in this simulator, so "disabled" means unreachable, same as the real service with no private endpoint configured. Still not simulated: virtual network rules, IP firewall rules, private endpoints and the networkAcls.defaultAction allow-list (which needs a real client network identity to match against — core/netsim models inter-VNet reachability, not a public-Internet client's source IP) and routingPreference.

azure.storage.encryption.title: Encryption (key source)
limitations: ENFORCED: selecting customer-managed keys requires a keyvaulturi + keyname and rejects (400) a keyvaulturi that doesn't name a Key Vault that actually exists in this subscription. The named key's own existence/enabled state INSIDE that vault is not checked (core/azure_arm_core.py has no reference to the Key Vault keys data-plane store), and every account is still encrypted the same way underneath — infrastructure (double) encryption and encryption scopes are not simulated.

azure.storage.dataprotection.title: Data protection (soft delete, point-in-time restore, versioning, change feed) over the blobServices/default ARM sub-resource
limitations: ENFORCED: Enable soft delete for blobs/containers really makes DELETE recoverable (invisible to normal listings, visible with include=deleted, restorable with comp=undelete, purged for real once the configured retention window elapses); Enable versioning for blobs really keeps an overwritten body as a separately fetchable version (?versionid=); Enable blob change feed really logs BlobCreated/BlobDeleted events from actual mutations. Still not enforced: operational backup (no backup engine), point-in-time restore, permanent delete, file-share soft delete (no Azure Files core) and version-level immutability.

azure.storage.locks.title: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to this storage account
limitations: Locks are only simulated at the resource scope (this account); subscription- and resource-group-scoped lock lists are an honest 'Not simulated' gap, same as the real Subscription/Resource group scope-switch buttons.

azure.storage.activitylog.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the 6-hours/30/90-day timespan picker are not modelled, and 'caller' is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

azure.storage.queues.title: Queues (create, list, delete) and messages (send, receive, peek, delete) over the Azure Storage Queue REST data plane
limitations: core/azure_queue_core.py keeps one global queue namespace per Nano instance (the same simplification the Key Vault keys/secrets stores make) — queues are not isolated per storage account, so two accounts share the same queue list.

azure.storage.diagnose.title: Diagnose and solve problems
limitations: Genuinely unmodellable: the real wizard's diagnosis comes from a proprietary, Microsoft-fleet-wide knowledge base and anomaly-detection model trained across millions of real customer incidents — there is no equivalent corpus, model or incident history a local simulator could stand in for, independent of how much telemetry Vyomi itself emits.

azure.storage.iam.title: Access control (IAM) scoped to a storage account
limitations: Check access really calls core/azure_iam_core.py's checkAccess evaluator scoped to THIS account's resource id (explicit-deny-wins, scope inheritance from the subscription/resource group); Role assignments/Deny assignments really filter the shared RBAC store to assignments whose scope covers this account, and new assignments are created scoped to it. Vyomi has no real directory, so principal IDs are free text (not validated against a tenant) and 'My access'/Classic administrators (a legacy pre-RBAC model) stay honest gaps.

azure.storage.datamigration.title: Data migration (AzCopy / Data Box / migration tooling)
limitations: This blade is a links-and-downloads page to external tooling, not an API Vyomi could intercept: AzCopy is a separately-installed CLI that already talks to the real Blob copy/upload operations this console's Containers page already exercises (nothing further to simulate there), and Data Box requires Microsoft to ship real physical hardware to a real address — genuinely impossible for a local simulator to run.

azure.storage.events.title: Events (Event Grid subscriptions on storage events)
limitations: NOT impossible, just not yet built this wave: core/azure_blob_core.py now derives real BlobCreated/BlobDeleted events (see azure.storage.dataprotection's change feed) that a storage-account-scoped Event Grid system topic could plausibly deliver, but core/azure_eventgrid_core.py's event subscriptions are currently modelled as a child of an Event Grid topic resource only, not a generic extension on any resource (the same shape azure_arm_core.py's locks/diagnosticSettings/metrics use) — wiring that generic scope and a real delivery target (e.g. a Vyomi queue) is a reasonable next step, deliberately deferred rather than rushed in this pass.

azure.storage.storagebrowser.title: Storage browser
limitations: A real master-detail view over the account's own containers and blobs (the same Blob REST calls the Containers page uses) — uploads, access tiers and SAS stay on the Containers/Blob pages rather than being duplicated here, same as the real portal's own cross-links.

azure.storage.storagemover.title: Storage Mover
limitations: This is a cross-link to a wholly separate resource provider (Microsoft.StorageMover: its own storage mover accounts, source/target endpoints, projects and on-premises migration agents) — not a storage-account sub-feature. Building it would mean a new product's own core, console pages and spec outside this storage service's scope, not a gap inside this one; a real on-premises agent to migrate FROM is also not something a local simulator has anything to connect to.

azure.storage.partnersolutions.title: Partner solutions
limitations: Third-party marketplace integrations (e.g. Cloudian, DataDynamics) — third-party identity and billing Vyomi cannot run.

azure.storage.fileshares.title: File shares (Azure Files)
limitations: Azure Files is a distinct SMB/NFS data plane (account.file.core.windows.net) with no core in this repo yet — not yet implemented.

azure.storage.tables.title: Table storage
limitations: core/azure_table_core.py models table create/list/delete and entity insert/get/query/replace/merge/delete over the native OData/JSON wire, in ONE global namespace per Nano instance (the same simplification Queues makes — tables are not isolated per storage account). $filter supports only `Field eq 'value'` terms joined by `and`; batch/transaction (EntityGroupTransaction), continuation-token paging and complex OData queries are not simulated.

azure.storage.frontdoorcdn.title: Front Door and CDN
limitations: A real CDN's value proposition is real global edge Points of Presence caching content close to real end users on the real Internet — a local simulator has exactly one place anything runs, so there is no second, distinct edge location for traffic to actually be routed through or cached at. A link-out to create/manage a genuinely separate Microsoft.Cdn/Microsoft.Network front-door resource, same reasoning as Storage Mover.

azure.storage.sas.title: Shared access signature (SAS) generation
limitations: The form builds a structurally correct SAS query string (sv/ss/srt/sp/st/se/spr/sig) from the selected options and signs it with the account's listKeys value, but core/azure_blob_core.py and core/azure_queue_core.py do not verify any request signature (SharedKey or SAS) — the generated token is not a real, checkable credential.

azure.storage.defender.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud
limitations: A separate security product (threat detection, vulnerability scanning) with its own billing plan — not modelled by any Vyomi core.

azure.storage.objectreplication.title: Object replication
limitations: Object replication policies (Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/objectReplicationPolicies, written to both accounts like Azure) are ENFORCED: a blob written to the source container that matches the rule's prefix filter is copied to the destination container, and deleting it removes the replica. Replication is synchronous (Azure's is asynchronous, minutes), only affects blobs written after the policy exists (no backfill), needs the destination container to exist, and does not require versioning/change feed or block writes to the destination container.

azure.storage.inventory.title: Blob inventory
limitations: ENFORCED: 'Run inventory now' really lists this account's current containers/blobs and writes a real CSV report blob into the configured destination container. Vyomi has no job scheduler, so this is on-demand rather than the real feature's daily/weekly scheduled run — the rule definition itself (scope, format, scheduling) is not stored or replayed.

azure.storage.staticwebsite.title: Static website hosting (properties.staticWebsite on blobServices/default)
limitations: Enforced: core/azure_blob_core.py serves the $web container's blobs (indexDocument for '/', errorDocument404Path on a miss) once staticWebsite.enabled is set. Served at a synthetic /{account}/__website__/ path rather than a distinct public hostname — this single-origin relay has no separate account.z#.web.core.windows.net host to route on.

azure.storage.lifecycle.title: Lifecycle management policies
limitations: Enforced, but lazily: core/azure_blob_core.py re-evaluates every enabled rule's prefixMatch filter against blob age on each list/get (not a daily background job) and applies the most aggressive matching baseBlob action (delete > tierToArchive > tierToCool), setting a real x-ms-access-tier / <AccessTier> or removing the blob. blobTypes beyond blockBlob, snapshot/version actions and the 'days after last access/creation' trigger variants are not modelled.

azure.storage.azureaisearch.title: Azure AI Search (index this storage account)
limitations: A cross-link to provisioning a wholly separate resource provider (Microsoft.Search/searchServices) with its own full-text/vector indexing pipeline and query language — building a real search engine (tokenization, ranking, vector similarity) is outside a storage account console's scope, the same reasoning as Storage Mover and Front Door/CDN.

azure.storage.datalakegen2upgrade.title: Data Lake Gen2 upgrade
limitations: ENFORCED: the upgrade really flips isHnsEnabled false→true on the account (core/azure_arm_core.py rejects it on an ineligible account kind, and rejects turning it back off — one-way, same as real Azure). Vyomi's blob core has no directory/path metadata to rewrite, so the real feature's full-container metadata migration has nothing to simulate — containers stay a flat namespace either way.

azure.storage.cors.title: Resource sharing (CORS) rules
limitations: Enforced for the Blob service only: core/azure_blob_core.py answers an OPTIONS preflight against the configured corsRules, denying (403 CorsPreflightFailure) any Origin/method/header combination that matches no rule and 200ing with real Access-Control-* headers for one that does. File/Queue/Table service CORS are honest gaps — Set/Get Service Properties isn't implemented on those data planes.

azure.storage.advisor.title: Advisor recommendations
limitations: Genuinely unmodellable: real Advisor recommendations (e.g. 'use reserved capacity', 'this account's redundancy is costlier than its access pattern needs') are trained on cost and usage PATTERNS aggregated across Microsoft's entire fleet of real customers over time — a single local simulator instance, even one that now emits real per-account metrics (see azure.storage.metrics), has no comparable fleet-wide population to analyse against.

azure.storage.insights.title: Insights (storage account metrics dashboards)
limitations: Shows the SAME real numbers as Metrics (UsedCapacity/BlobCount/ContainerCount/Transactions/Ingress/Egress, derived from this account's own activity) as an at-a-glance dashboard rather than a historical chart — Vyomi keeps a single current value, not a time series.

azure.storage.alerts.title: Alerts
limitations: Alert rules are real Microsoft.Insights/metricAlerts resources scoped to this account (properties.scopes); the console evaluates each rule's criteria against the account's REAL current metric value to show Fired/OK. There is no background evaluation loop or notification delivery (action groups aren't wired) — the status is only (re)computed when the page is viewed, the same lazy-evaluation simplification Lifecycle makes.

azure.storage.metrics.title: Metrics
limitations: ENFORCED over the real native Microsoft.Insights/metrics wire: UsedCapacity/BlobCount/ContainerCount are computed live from the account's actual containers/blobs, and Transactions/Ingress/Egress are real per-account counters bumped by every Blob data-plane request core/azure_blob_core.py serves. A single current-value data point, not a persisted historical time series; Availability and SuccessE2ELatency are not modelled (Vyomi has no transient failures or network latency to measure).

azure.storage.workbooks.title: Workbooks
limitations: Workbooks are real Microsoft.Insights/workbooks ARM resources scoped to this account (sourceId); opening one re-renders the REAL current value of its pinned metric. Not a KQL/query-step authoring canvas — one metric per workbook, no visualizations gallery.

azure.storage.diagnostics.title: Diagnostic settings
limitations: Diagnostic settings are real Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings ARM extension resources scoped to this account; a storageAccountId destination must name a storage account that actually exists (400 otherwise). Enabling a log category here REALLY GATES what Logs shows for this account (see azure.storage.logs) — but logs are captured in-memory by core/azure_blob_core.py and read back through this console's own Logs page, not actually delivered to the configured workspace/storage account/event hub (no Log Analytics/Event Hub ingestion engine exists).

azure.storage.logs.title: Logs (Log Analytics queries over storage diagnostics)
limitations: A real field filter over this account's real, in-memory request log (core/azure_blob_core.py), gated by which log categories an actual Diagnostic setting on this account has enabled — not a KQL/Log Analytics workspace query engine, and nothing is persisted once the Nano instance/appliance restarts.

azure.storage.tasks.title: Tasks (Azure Automation runbooks)
limitations: Genuinely unsafe/impossible to simulate generically: a real Storage task/Automation runbook executes arbitrary customer-authored PowerShell/Python on a separate managed worker fleet — faithfully simulating it means running untrusted arbitrary code, which this simulator deliberately does not do anywhere (every other 'task'-like feature here — Lifecycle, Blob inventory — is a fixed, bounded operation Vyomi implements directly, not an arbitrary script host).

azure.storage.exporttemplate.title: Export template (ARM/Bicep/Terraform generated client-side from this resource)
limitations: Download, Add to library, Deploy and Visualize template are honest 'Not simulated' actions — only template generation from the account's current ARM properties is real.

azure.storage.support.title: Support + Troubleshooting
limitations: Opens a real Microsoft support ticket workflow — outside what a local simulator can run.
